title: Semilinear tensor transport through a ring presentation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in the common sheaf-value universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, so $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $T=Y,X$ for the two topoi. Let $D_T\to A_T$ and $D_T\to B_T$ be maps of commutative ring sheaves, let $R_T$ be another commutative ring sheaf, and supply ring isomorphisms
$$\beta_T:A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T\xrightarrow{\sim}R_T.$$
Suppose $d:f^{-1}D_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X$, $a:f^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$, $b:f^{-1}B_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X$, and $c:f^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X$ are ring isomorphisms. Assume $a,b$ commute with the two $D$-algebra structure maps over $d$, and
$$c f^{-1}\beta_Y=\beta_X(a\otimes b)\sigma_f,$$
where $\sigma_f:f^{-1}(A_Y\otimes_{D_Y}B_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}A_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}D_Y}f^{-1}B_Y$ is the canonical pure-tensor inverse-image comparison.

For $A_T$-module sheaves $M_T$ let $s:f^{-1}M_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}M_X$ be an additive isomorphism semilinear over $a$. Give $N_T=M_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T$ the $R_T$-action transported by $\beta_T$ from
$$(x\otimes b_0)(m\otimes b_1)=xm\otimes b_0b_1.$$
Then there is a unique additive isomorphism
$$r:f^{-1}N_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}N_X$$
whose adjunct is $m\otimes v\mapsto\widetilde s(m)\otimes\widetilde b(v)$, where $\widetilde s:M_Y\to f_*M_X$ and $\widetilde b:B_Y\to f_*B_X$ are the actual adjoints of $s,b$, and the target tensor is mapped into $f_*N_X$ by the sectionwise tensor pairing. It is semilinear over $c$: $r(z n)=c(z)r(n)$ for local sections of $f^{-1}R_Y$ and $f^{-1}N_Y$.

This construction is natural under compatible changes of $B$ and $R$: if $B'_T,R'_T,\beta'_T,b',c'$ satisfy the same assumptions, $q_T:B_T\to B'_T$ are $D_T$-algebra maps, $i_T:R_T\to R'_T$ obey $i_T\beta_T=\beta'_T(1\otimes q_T)$, and $b'f^{-1}q_Y=q_Xb$, $c'f^{-1}i_Y=i_Xc$, then with $j_T=1_{M_T}\otimes q_T$ the resulting maps satisfy
$$r' f^{-1}j_Y=j_Xr.$$
There is no local-freeness, finiteness, completeness, or existence of points hypothesis on these module sheaves or topoi.

source.place: Integral twist paragraph, module structure and inverse image of the tensor line; abstract sheaf-theoretic transport argument underlying old step 3 (tensor isomorphism and semilinearity) and step 5 (coefficient naturality) of lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image, serving prop-weil-twist-preserves proof's final integral scalar-extension sentence.

proof.text: Put $F=f^{-1}$, $V=f_*$ and $D'=FD_Y$. Transport the ring and module operations through the finite-product comparisons of $F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport] with $R=D_Y$, $A=S=D'$ and structural map the identity. This gives the actual algebraic inverse image $I$ and its module adjunction with underlying adjunction $F\dashv V$; it satisfies [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. In particular its actions are the transported actions, rather than independently chosen ones. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to get natural isomorphisms $\sigma_{P,Q}:F(P\otimes_{D_Y}Q)\simeq FP\otimes_{D'}FQ$. Its normalization is an equality of pairing morphisms: $\sigma_{P,Q}F(p_{P,Q})=p_{FP,FQ}\kappa$, where $p$ denotes the pure pairing and $\kappa:F(P\times Q)\simeq FP\times FQ$. Indeed take the test sheaf $P\times Q$ and its two projections in the cited generalized-section assertion. Thus this equality applies to the full product sheaf, with no assertion that sections of an inverse image come from sections downstairs.

Write $\otimes_p$ for the sectionwise presheaf tensor, so that $X\otimes_{D_T}Y$ is the abelian-group sheafification of $X\otimes_pY$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The ring sheaf $A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T$ of the statement is the ring sheafification of the presheaf of commutative rings $P_T=A_T\otimes_pB_T$, $P_T(U)=A_T(U)\otimes_{D_T(U)}B_T(U)$. For each $U$, $M_T(U)\otimes_{D_T(U)}B_T(U)$ is an ordinary $P_T(U)$-module by $(x\otimes v)(m\otimes w)=xm\otimes vw$: the formula is additive in each variable, and the two balancing checks $(\delta x)m\otimes vw=xm\otimes(\delta v)w$ and $x(\delta m)\otimes vw=xm\otimes v(\delta w)$ are the $D_T(U)$-tensor relation; associativity $(xx')m\otimes(vv')w=x(x'm)\otimes v(v'w)$ and the unit $1m\otimes1w=m\otimes w$ hold on pure inputs. Restrictions preserve the formula, so $M_T\otimes_pB_T$ is a presheaf of $P_T$-modules. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] its abelian sheafification $N_T$ carries a unique map $(A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_T)\times N_T\to N_T$ compatible with this presheaf action, and it is a module action. Pulling it back along $\beta_T^{-1}$ gives exactly the stated $R_T$-action. Below, an action or a linear map is identified by the same lemma: by its uniqueness clause, and by its factorization clause (a $P$-linear presheaf map out of a presheaf module factors uniquely through a $P^\#$-linear map out of its sheafification, whose underlying additive map is the abelian factorization). [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] is used for maps out of a two-factor tensor.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) and Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), presheaf tensor and its sheafification

proof.text: The restriction of $s$ to $D'$ is semilinear over $d$: apply the compatibility of $a$ with the $D$-algebra structure map to its stated $a$-semilinearity. Similarly $b$ is semilinear over $d$. Regard $N_X$ as a $D'$-module via $d$. The pairing $(u,v)\mapsto s(u)\otimes b(v)$ is $D'$-bilinear: for $\delta\in D'$, $s(\delta u)\otimes b(v)=d(\delta)s(u)\otimes b(v)=s(u)\otimes d(\delta)b(v)=s(u)\otimes b(\delta v)$. The universal property gives $U:FM_Y\otimes_{D'}FB_Y\to N_X$. The inverse pairing $m\otimes w\mapsto s^{-1}(m)\otimes b^{-1}(w)$ is balanced using $d^{-1}$; its two composites with $U$ are the identity on pure pairs, hence are identities by uniqueness. Define $r=U\sigma_{M_Y,B_Y}$. Both factors are additive isomorphisms, so $r$ is one as well.

Let $\eta$ be the actual unit of $F\dashv V$. Set $\widetilde s=V(s)\eta_{M_Y}$ and $\widetilde b=V(b)\eta_{B_Y}$. Equip $VN_X$ with its $D_Y$-module structure through the adjunct of $d$, using [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport] with structural map $d:D'\to D_X$. Its operation and mate equations say that the pairing $h_0(m,v)=V(p_{M_X,B_X})(\widetilde s(m),\widetilde b(v))$ is $D_Y$-bilinear. Hence [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] gives a map $h:N_Y\to VN_X$. Now the adjunct of $r$, composed with $p_{M_Y,B_Y}$, is
$$V(r)\eta_{N_Y}p_{M_Y,B_Y}=V(rF(p_{M_Y,B_Y}))\eta_{M_Y\times B_Y}=V(p_{M_X,B_X})(\widetilde s\times\widetilde b).$$
The first equality is unit naturality; the second uses step 1's pairing identity and step 3's formula for $U$. For the products, the two projections of $V(\kappa)\eta_{M_Y\times B_Y}$ are precisely $\eta_{M_Y}$ and $\eta_{B_Y}$ by unit naturality; this justifies the displayed product notation for arbitrary geometric morphisms. The module adjunction in the cited transport lemma makes this adjunct $D_Y$-linear. The universal property therefore identifies it with $h$, which is the required actual-adjoint formula.

The adjunct formula also implies uniqueness among additive maps, without assuming their scalar compatibility in advance. If two such maps have the specified adjunct values on $m\otimes v$, their adjuncts agree after precomposition with the presheaf tensor on every object: every algebraic tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors and both maps are additive. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $N_Y$ is the abelian-group sheafification of this presheaf tensor. Its abelian-group sheafification universal property makes the two adjuncts equal. Injectivity of the given adjunction hom equivalence makes the original maps equal. This argument uses no claim that every section of the sheafified tensor is a global sum of pure sections.

Write $A'=FA_Y$, $B'=FB_Y$, $M'=FM_Y$, $S'=A'\otimes_{D'}B'$ and $N'=M'\otimes_{D'}B'$; $S'$ is the ring sheafification of $P'=A'\otimes_pB'$ and $N'$ the sheafification of the presheaf $P'$-module $M'\otimes_pB'$, as in step 2. Give $FN_Y$ the $S'$-action transported from $F$ of the $F(A_Y\otimes_{D_Y}B_Y)$-action through $\sigma_{A_Y,B_Y}$ and the finite-product comparison; it is additive in each variable. We show that $\sigma^{-1}=\sigma_{M_Y,B_Y}^{-1}:N'\to FN_Y$ is $S'$-linear. Apply $F$ to the four-variable pairing identity of step 2 (action of $p_{A_Y,B_Y}(x,v)$ on $p_{M_Y,B_Y}(u,w)$ equals $p_{M_Y,B_Y}(xu,vw)$), identify its finite products, and substitute the pairing-morphism identities of step 1 twice. The transported $A'$-action on $M'$ and multiplication on $B'$ are exactly $F$ of the original operations by [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. This yields, as an equality of sheaf maps on $A'\times B'\times M'\times B'$, $(x\otimes v)\cdot\sigma^{-1}(u\otimes w)=\sigma^{-1}(xu\otimes vw)$. Hence the presheaf map $M'\otimes_pB'\to FN_Y$, $u\otimes w\mapsto\sigma^{-1}(u\otimes w)$, well defined and additive by the universal property of each ordinary tensor, is $P'$-linear on finite sums of pure tensors. By the factorization clause of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] it factors through an $S'$-linear map $N'\to FN_Y$; its underlying additive map agrees with the additive $\sigma^{-1}$ on the presheaf, so equals it by abelian uniqueness. Thus $\sigma_{M_Y,B_Y}$ intertwines the two actions. In particular $FN_Y$ has the $FR_Y$-action obtained from this $S'$-action by $F\beta_Y\,\sigma_{A_Y,B_Y}^{-1}$.

Set $t=a\otimes b:S'\to A_X\otimes_{D_X}B_X$, a ring map, and regard $N_X$ as an $S'$-module through $t$ and the step-2 action. On pure inputs over any object the definitions and semilinearity of $s$ give $$s(xu)\otimes b(vw)=a(x)s(u)\otimes b(v)b(w)=t(x\otimes v)\,(s(u)\otimes b(w)).$$ So the presheaf map $M'\otimes_pB'\to N_X$, $u\otimes w\mapsto s(u)\otimes b(w)$, is $P'$-linear on finite sums of pure tensors. By the factorization clause of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] it factors through an $S'$-linear map $N'\to N_X$, whose underlying additive map agrees with $U$ of step 3 on the presheaf and therefore equals $U$. Hence $U(\zeta n)=t(\zeta)U(n)$ for local sections $\zeta$ of $S'$ and $n$ of $N'$. Step 6 and the hypothesis $cF\beta_Y=\beta_Xt\sigma_{A_Y,B_Y}$ now give $r(zn)=c(z)r(n)$: put $\zeta=\sigma_{A_Y,B_Y}(F\beta_Y)^{-1}(z)$; the ring equation gives $c(z)=\beta_Xt(\zeta)$, and step 6 followed by the preceding identity gives $r(zn)=U(\zeta\,\sigma_{M_Y,B_Y}n)=t(\zeta)r(n)$, which is $\beta_Xt(\zeta)r(n)$ in the $R_X$-action. No representation of $z$ by a single pure tensor is required.

proof.text: Finally use the primed data of the coefficient-change clause. Naturality of the comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] gives $\sigma_{M_Y,B'_Y}Fj_Y=(1\otimes Fq_Y)\sigma_{M_Y,B_Y}$. On a pure pair $(u,v)$ the two maps $U'(1\otimes Fq_Y)$ and $j_XU$ have values $s(u)\otimes b'Fq_Y(v)$ and $s(u)\otimes q_Xb(v)$; these are equal by the assumed coefficient square. They are $D'$-linear, so [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] makes them equal. Composing the comparison equation yields $r'Fj_Y=j_Xr$. The equations $i_T\beta_T=\beta'_T(1\otimes q_T)$ show that this is an equation of maps compatible with the scalar structures: the presheaf map $m\otimes w\mapsto m\otimes q_T(w)$ from $M_T\otimes_pB_T$ to $N'_T$ (an $A_T\otimes_pB_T$-module through $1\otimes q_T$) is linear on pure inputs, where both sides of $(x\otimes v)(m\otimes w)\mapsto xm\otimes q_T(v)q_T(w)$ agree; by the factorization clause of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] $j_T$ is semilinear over $1\otimes q_T$, hence over $i_T$, and $c'Fi_Y=i_Xc$ identifies the scalar structures on both sides. Only the stated ring and module laws, small-site tensor constructions, and the geometric adjunction have been used.
